Hi John —

Thanks again for taking the demo with Neha and me this morning. Quick recap and next steps from our side so we can align on capacity and SLAs: 

What we heard on the call:
- Target P95 latency: 350–400ms for text-generation at a typical prompt length of ~120 tokens.
- Average request size: ~120 tokens in, ~40 tokens out.
- Expected sustained QPS: 35–45 requests/sec across your service (peak bursts up to ~120 r/s during campaign spikes).
- Concurrency model: you need ~60 concurrent model calls (parallel requests) from multiple microservices; you also expect long-lived streaming sessions (~10–20s per session) for transcript-style flows.
- Connection pooling: you’d like >=200 simultaneous HTTP connections from your edge fleet.

Actions we’ll take:
1) I attached a quota/proposal PDF and an SLO matrix spreadsheet with two options: Reserved Dedicated pool (predictable latency + higher concurrency) and Hosted with quota bump + graceful degradation (cheaper but with fallback).
2) Neha will share a short tuning guide for streaming sessions and recommended keep-alive settings.
3) We’ll propose an initial concurrency quota and a bump path based on observed sampling in the first 30 days.

Next steps for Acme:
- Confirm whether P95 400ms is an absolute must or a target we can iterate on (reply here).
- Share the procurement contact (if different from procurement@acme.com) so we can put together a formal quote.

I’ve attached the proposal (redwood-quota-proposal-ACME.pdf) and the SLO matrix. I’ll follow up with concrete quota numbers in the next email after Neha’s assessment.

Best,

Thanks Marissa — solid recap. A couple of clarifications: 

- P95 400ms is the bar our product team wants to hit for the web UI. For internal async jobs we can accept higher latency, but for the UI it’s critical.
- The 120 r/s burst is accurate during marketing peaks; sustained is probably closer to 40.
- On concurrency: when you say ~60 concurrent model calls, does that account for streaming sessions? Our streaming sessions typically hold a connection open and appear as active calls for the duration. We’re worried about connection limits more than token throughput.

Hi John — quick technical notes that address the streaming + concurrency callouts: 

- Streaming sessions count toward concurrent model invocations while the stream is active. For planning, treat a stream as 1 active request per open session. If you expect 200 concurrent streaming sessions during peak, that is 200 concurrent model invocations.
- Redwood’s Hosted tier enforces per-account rate limits (requests/sec) and concurrency quotas. For Acme’s numbers, two practical options:
  1) Hosted with quota increase: we can raise your per-second quota to 250 r/s with a concurrency soft limit of 200. Soft limits allow brief bursts but are monitored; in case of sustained overage requests may be throttled.
  2) Dedicated Reserved pool: provision a dedicated GPU pool sized to guarantee P95 <400ms at your expected peak concurrency. This comes with a committed monthly cost but provides predictable tail latency and higher connection throughput (we can support >500 concurrent streams depending on instance sizing).

- Connection pooling: for Hosted we recommend HTTP keep-alive and a client-side pool of 50–100 connections per host to ensure TLS reuse. For Dedicated, you can colocate a connection proxy in your VPC to aggregate connections (reduces client-side pool requirements).

I attached an SLO matrix and an initial quota proposal (redwood-quota-proposal-ACME.pdf and slo-matrix-acme.xlsx). The attached proposal includes a stepped quota plan: initial soft quota (250 r/s, 200 concurrency) with a committed path to Dedicated if sustained usage exceeds thresholds for two consecutive weeks.

If you can share a short traffic sample (1 hour trace or aggregated RPS histogram), I can give a tighter sizing recommendation.

Thanks,
Neha
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
